newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth buys wireless operations in South.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth buys wireless operations in South.

text.p: BellSouth Corp said Wednesday it signed a definitive agreement to acquire wireless cable operations and assets in up to nine Southern markets from American Telecasting Inc.
BellSouth said it agreed to pay no less than $67.9 million and no more than $103.2 million, with the closing price dependent on the total number of channel leases and licenses delivered at closing.

The agreement, still subject to regulatory approval, will give BellSouth rights to provide wireless cable service in six Florida markets -- Jacksonville, Orlando, Daytona Beach, Ft. Myers, Lakeland and Bradenton -- as well as Louisville, Ky.

As part of the pact, BellSouth would acquire American's existing operations in those markets, which serve over 35,000 existing customers. Also it would buy all of American's assets in those markets, including the rights to wireless cable licenses, and certain additional channel rights.
The company said the nine markets comprise a total of about two million line-of-sight households, which is the industry measurement for potential customers served.
The companies agreed on options that give them up to 24 months to reach a decision on the sale of American assets in two additional markets: Naples, Fla., and Sebring, Fla.
BellSouth said it plans to use digital wireless cable to provide more than 100 channels of programming, including national satellite programming and existing local broadcast channels.
